title: userpictures own-picture exception lets a caller read another user's avatar thumbnail by naming it as their own picture

labels.name: php
labels.description: Pull requests that update php code

body:
Found by the Opus design review for PR #919 (#905), 2026-10-13, from code reading at #919's head `96f293e5`. The defect exists on master too. Not reproduced over HTTP yet.

`FilesApiController::CheckGroupReadPermission` (`~:207-216`) lets a caller read a `userpictures` file without `USERS_READ` when the requested name equals their own `users.picture_file_name` and no other user claims that exact name. `picture_file_name` is written verbatim (`UsersApiController.php ~:337-339`; the code says so at `~:191-195`), and picture derivatives are named `<name>__downscaledto<h>x<w>.<ext>`.

## Failure scenario

1. User V's avatar `V.png` renders in the nav bar (`views/layout/default.blade.php:520`), which creates `V__downscaledto32x32.png`.
2. A caller holding only `USERS_EDIT_SELF` sets their own `picture_file_name` to `V__downscaledto32x32.png`. No other row claims that exact name.
3. `GET /api/files/userpictures/<base64 of that name>` passes the own-picture exception, so the caller reads V's avatar thumbnail without `USERS_READ`.

## Done when

- [ ] The own-picture exception applies only to a name without the derivative infix (`FilesService::DOWNSCALED_INFIX`), and it authorizes derivatives through their root original. Alternatively, `picture_file_name` writes refuse the infix, which is a write-side change.
- [ ] A regression test covers the scenario above.

Related: #905, #919, #920.
